objective: Change E_t's schema as ruled in R10 (a) to (d), so that a verdict is not widened or narrowed by the schema instead of by the evidence: human-seat loop ids, an attribution field on acceptance rows, a distinct pending status, and out-of-scope ids declared beside the unrunnable ones.
tasks: (a) widen the loop id pattern to admit human-seat ids; the exact form is the developer's
(b) add no new status value; record attribution as an order field on the acceptance row, order: shown | attributed, required on met rows and failing closed
(c) make pending its own status, so a verdict row with any pending item is undefined and never would-not-merge
(d) declare out-of-scope ids in the same parseable block as R3's unrunnable ids, at the criteria SHA, before any candidate, excluded from the verdict, with the two lists kept separate
keep BE-1.3 in this part: the runtime refuses an E_t whose loop is not the run's
supply the validator the QA seat runs, not a writer: the QA seat writes E_t
out_of_scope: a writer for E_t (BE-7: the QA seat writes it)
the shadow merge gate, which keys on what this makes recordable
B part 1, the G-042 repair, which is already merged
preserve: candidate A's accepted behaviour, including the configwatch R95 and R96 rows, and R77 stopping before git
every existing E_t consumer, each named with how it reads the new fields
backward compatibility (BE-5): an existing E_t still validates
